prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has knee injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1195; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you were involved in at an intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state where you were driving and where you were headed when the collision occurred.

A: I was driving westbound on the main road, heading toward the grocery store near my home. I was in the right lane and had just come to a stop behind a car at the light.

Q: Can you describe what happened next?

A: The light was red, so I had stopped. Then I felt a hard impact from behind. My head snapped forward and then back, and my car was pushed into the vehicle in front of me.

Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?

A: No, I was looking at the light and my mirrors didn't show anything close. I only heard the tires and then the crash.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Have you noticed any injuries since the collision?

A: My right knee hit the dashboard. It's swollen and painful, especially when I bend it or stand up for a long time. I went to urgent care the same day and they took X-rays.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or specialist since then?

A: I have an appointment with an orthopedic doctor next week. They told me it could be a ligament or cartilage problem.

Q: Did you have any prior problems with that knee before this collision?

A: No, nothing serious. I had some minor soreness a few years ago after exercising, but I never needed treatment for it.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: I just want to make sure my medical bills and the repairs to my car get covered. I'm still having trouble driving comfortably.

Q: Thank you. That concludes this recorded statement.
